outcome_intro: Ask your AI "which machines went dark this week?" or "which customer needs attention first?" and get one answer across every ThreatDown OneView site. OneView answers one site at a time, and its endpoint searches only take explicit account IDs. This skill resolves every site for you, ranks site health, reconciles seats, and previews isolations, scans and reboots before any job is sent.

instead_of_say.say: Which endpoints haven't checked in for a day, across all my sites?

instead_of_say.instead: Clicking through every customer site in OneView to see who has infected, isolated, unprotected or reboot-pending machines
Looking up a machine's site and endpoint ID, then hand-building a jobs request to isolate it

pain_points: OneView's endpoint search is a POST that needs an explicit list of account IDs, so a cross-site question like "what went dark since Friday" means listing sites, collecting each site's account ID and paging 2,000 rows at a time. ThreatDown's own answer is a PowerShell script in a support article.

Site health lives on separate pages and filters: infected, suspicious, isolated, unprotected, reboot-pending and not-scanned machines are each a different view, so deciding which customer needs you first takes a click-through of every site.

Seat allocations live on each site's subscription while deployed and recently seen machines live on the Endpoints page, so catching an over- or under-allocated site before billing is a spreadsheet job.
A scan or isolation sent to an offline machine sits waiting or quietly expires, and nothing tells you which jobs never ran.

different_vs_wrappers: We found no other MCP server for ThreatDown OneView on GitHub as of October 2026. The integrations that do exist, such as the [Sumo Logic](https://help.sumologic.com/docs/platform-services/automation-service/app-central/integrations/threatdown-oneview) and [Datadog (Crest Data)](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/crest-data-systems-threatdown-oneview/) apps, move OneView data into a SIEM or monitoring tool, and community scripts like [nebula2nebula](https://github.com/B10sp4rt4n/nebula2nebula) target migrations. This skill fans every question out across all your sites, syncs sites, endpoints, detections and jobs into a local SQLite mirror, and previews every response job before it is sent.
different_vs_vendor: ThreatDown's own AI features, such as the AI-assisted Security Advisor and AI Detection & Response, work inside the ThreatDown console. This skill complements them by bringing every OneView site into the AI agent you already use, answering cross-site questions in one command without replacing OneView.

faqs.a: Yes, on paid ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS, so you expose the local ThreatDown MCP server via a secure bridge. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You enter your credentials once.
Your data stays on your machine. The CLI, MCP server, and the local mirror are all local. The AI sees query results, not raw bulk data, and credentials are never bundled or transmitted by MSP Skills.
Free. Apache-2.0 licensed. You pay only for whichever AI agent you already use.

faqs.q: Is this for ThreatDown OneView or ThreatDown Nebula?
faqs.a: OneView, the multi-site console ThreatDown (Malwarebytes) gives MSPs. It talks to the OneView API at api.threatdown.com/oneview and works across every site you manage. A single-company Nebula console is not a OneView account; it uses a different API, which this skill does not cover.

An OAuth client ID and secret from OneView: open Integrate in the left menu, click Add, name the app and tick the scopes. ThreatDown says a Global or Site Administrator has to create it, and the secret is shown only once. Read covers every report; the respond commands (isolate, restore, scan, reboot, update) also need execute, and other changes need write. Set THREATDOWN_CLIENT_ID and THREATDOWN_CLIENT_SECRET, then run threatdown-cli doctor.

faqs.q: Can my AI isolate or scan client machines?
faqs.a: Only through commands you allow. The respond commands preview by default: they list the machines that would get the job and send nothing until you add --confirm (or the global --yes), and they refuse more than 25 endpoints unless you raise --max-targets. Other paths send immediately: endpoint-jobs issue, endpoint-jobs bulk-issue, grid jobs-bulk, import endpoint_jobs, and the MCP server's generic threatdown_execute tool. For a reporting agent, create the OAuth client with read only, or set THREATDOWN_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 so the MCP server drops its write tools and refuses every non-GET call through threatdown_execute.

faqs.q: Has it been tested against a live OneView tenant?
faqs.a: Not yet. Every command was built from ThreatDown's published OneView API specification and tested against a local mock of that API, not a real tenant. If you run it against your own OneView account, tell us what worked or broke on the GitHub issue tracker or at a Build Session; a real MSP run is what earns the live-verified badge.

faqs.q: Will this replace the OneView console?
faqs.a: No. OneView stays where you set policies, manage subscriptions and deploy agents. This skill answers cross-site reporting and triage questions from your AI agent or terminal, and sends response jobs you have previewed.

governance_summary: The skill is read-first: the fleet reports, seat reconciliation, threat triage, customer report, sync, search and every list, get and search command are read-only and safe to let an agent run. The respond commands send isolation, restore, scan, reboot and update jobs to real machines but preview until you add --confirm; the raw job commands (endpoint-jobs issue, grid jobs-bulk), import endpoint_jobs and the MCP server's generic threatdown_execute tool send immediately, so keep them human-in-the-loop or set THREATDOWN_MCP_READ_ONLY=1. The scopes you tick on the OneView OAuth client (read, write, execute) are the outer limit on anything an agent can do.
